exactness_argument: The online scan and the rank stage call the same search, extract128::<CANON_LIFT, ORDER_FEISTEL, P> on one target point: the same folded index, the same Feistel state order keyed by the target's public hash, the same per-state candidates (shift outer, stored root inner), and a return at the first lifted relation. The online scan is a first hit for one target Q; a rank attempt is a first hit for one target [a]G - R_j. Only the probe loop P differs: PIPE_COMPACT (the S3 loop: x(R_{k,s}) mapped to the polynomial basis and the two roots of the third summation polynomial S3(x(R_{k,s}), x(T), X) solved in a batch) or PIPE_FRAME (the rank stage's loop). E is defined over F_2, so phi(x, y) = (x^2, y^2) is a group automorphism and T +- phi^s(R_k) = phi^s(T_s +- R_k) with T_s = phi^(-s)(T); the roots of S3(x(R_{k,s}), x(T), X) are exactly x(T + R_{k,s}) and x(T - R_{k,s}). The frame loop computes these two field elements by point addition from (x, y) of R_k and of T_s (tabulated once per target) and applies phi^s as a rotation of the normal-basis word, so each candidate's two partner words, canonical keys and shifts are the S3 loop's, possibly in the other order. The exceptional inputs (x(R_k) = x(T_s), x(R_k) = 0, x(T_s) = 0) and roots failing the curve check go to the S3 solver exactly as in the S3 loop. At a root-table hit the frame loop forms the S3 input, solves it and evaluates the pair in the S3 order at the S3 loop's probe positions, so the first lifted relation, its probe count, root calls and relation checks are the S3 loop's. This is the rank-probe experiment's exactness result for PIPE_FRAME against PIPE_COMPACT (its tests and four Tier 1 rank blocks), applied to the online target; here it is tested on a 9-orbit base through extract128, and cFX compares the S3 loop with the frame loop on every state of every scan it runs.

statistics.end_to_end_secondary: E2E(c) = K + mean over the points of cold_in_process_ms(c), with the SAME shared rank stage K = timing_ms.rank_stage of the one kP process in the numerator and the denominator (the reasoning of koblitz-n83-indexlift-20261019, origin/claude/n83-indexlift, README 'The rank stage: shared, and why': the rank stage runs identical code over an identical index, so its cost is not a treatment effect, and per-arm rank processes would add only their process drift; here the rank stage's code is byte for byte the rank-probe producer's and KIC_ONLINE_SOLVE is read only by the online scan). R_e2e = E2E(cS) / E2E(cF); bootstrap 10,000 draws, seed 20261021: kP's 600 attempts resampled (its non-attempt time kept) and the points resampled, paired across cS and cF. Expected about 1.0006 (0.1 s of about 166 s); end-to-end regression iff its upper bound < 1

Bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 20261020: the points resampled with replacement, paired across cS and cF; percentile 95% interval

success_criterion: AGENTS.md, 'Success criterion: iterative improvement of the index-calculus baseline': "the success criterion is a verified, measured improvement over the current index-calculus baseline. Every such improvement is a success and is reported as one." and, under 'Improvement': "A stage-level win is reported as a stage improvement and becomes a pipeline improvement once it moves end-to-end `S`."
success_criterion_reading: The primary decides a stage improvement of the online phase. Under the quoted rule an online improvement (primary lower bound > 1) is a verified, measured improvement over the baseline and a success; with no end-to-end regression (end-to-end secondary upper bound >= 1) it improves the baseline row's online S and online gap to rho and is recorded as a stage improvement. It is reported as a pipeline improvement only if the end-to-end secondary's lower bound also exceeds 1 ('once it moves end-to-end S'). An end-to-end regression (upper bound < 1) blocks promotion.
